name: Forward Step-Up
definition: A lead-limb closed-chain compound step in which the lead foot begins on a raised platform while the athlete raises the body to a brief bilateral standing position on that platform without pushing off or hopping from the trail leg. The trail foot then returns to the lower floor, followed by the lead foot; replacing the same lead foot on the platform resets the next repetition. The initial roster owns only the exact 21-centimeter bodyweight forward stepping sequence studied with three-dimensional hip, knee, and ankle kinematics and kinetics. It does not generalize that geometry to a gym-style continuous set that leaves the lead foot on the platform, arbitrary box heights, external loads, a hovering trail foot, continuous stair climbing, step-downs, or lateral, crossover, diagonal, reverse, explosive, or machine-stepping tasks. The fixed lunge pattern is Vivobody's broader app-level classification for unilateral asymmetric-support lower-body compounds; the family ID names the raised-lead-foot geometry that distinguishes this task from a stationary split squat or dynamic lunge.

variantAxes.description: The lead-limb chain relationship: the load-bearing lead foot remains fixed on the platform through the loaded ascent and trail-foot descent, then steps down to finish the full sequence. This value does not claim that the trail foot is fixed.
The gross whole-body posture at the lower start and upper endpoint.
Whether an external surface supports the torso; the reviewed task permitted a safety bar for balance emergencies but instructed no propulsive assistance.
The asymmetric support topology at the loaded start; the lead foot is already on a raised platform while the trail foot is on the lower floor.
The direction from the lower floor toward the platform relative to the athlete.
The vertical difference between the lower floor and platform; the active fixture pins Wang et al.'s 21-centimeter step.
The lead foot remains on the platform through ascent and trail-foot descent, then steps to the lower floor after the trail foot as the studied sequence ends.
The trail foot's deliberate within-repetition transition; it moves from the lower floor to the platform and returns to the lower floor before the lead foot steps down.
Whether the lower trail leg may push or hop to create the ascent; Wang et al. explicitly prohibited both.
The reviewed upper endpoint and support phase before descent.
Whether an external implement is placed on the athlete; the active fixture is bodyweight-only.
The reviewed endpoint convention from the raised-lead-foot start to bilateral standing on the platform and then bilateral standing on the lower floor.
The source did not standardize a numeric trunk or spinal path; deliberate spinal motion is not a prime action, but measured segment motion is not claimed to be zero.
The dynamic concentric lead-hip action during ascent.
The dynamic concentric lead-knee action during ascent.
The dynamic lead-ankle motion from the dorsiflexed lower position toward the standing-on-platform angle during ascent.
Whether deliberate toe motion, inversion, or eversion creates the repetition; transition of the whole trail foot is recorded separately.
The whole-task contact pattern: the lead foot loads the platform through ascent and trail-foot descent, then both feet finish on the lower floor.
The reset required after the studied sequence ends with both feet on the lower floor; the same lead foot is replaced fully on the platform before the next repetition.
Whether a seat, pad, rail, or other external support receives the athlete between repetitions; ordinary foot-floor support does not count as an external reset.
Which lead-limb joint motions deliberately create the concentric ascent.

execution.startingPosition: Stand facing a platform exactly 21 centimeters above the lower floor with the lead foot placed fully on top and the trail foot on the lower floor.
execution.movement: Shift onto the lead leg. Push through the lead foot and straighten that hip and knee until the other foot reaches the platform beside it.
execution.endpoint: Pause briefly with both feet on the platform.
execution.returnPhase: Shift back onto the lead leg, return the trail foot to the lower floor, and step the lead foot down beside it to complete the repetition. Replace the same lead foot fully on the platform before the next repetition.
execution.controlledJoints: Do not push or hop from the trail leg.
execution.supportAndPosture: Stand upright and use no hand support for the step.
disqualifyingCompensations: Pushing off or hopping from the trail leg turns the lead-leg step-up into a two-leg jump.
Leaving the lead foot on the platform between repetitions turns the full sequence into a continuous gym-style step-up.
Pulling on a rail for help turns the unsupported step-up into an assisted step.
execution.sideOrDirection: Switch lead sides after the set.
